title: Workflow definition (workflows/<id>.yml)
description: Which agents run, in what order, for one kind of change. Before these files the answer lived only inside orchestrator/src/classification/taskClassifier.ts, so 'what happens for a hotfix' was a code change rather than something a person could read or edit. The classifier remains the runtime authority (it is a pure function and must not read files at import time); these files state the same thing in checkable form, and --check-workflows fails when the two disagree.

workflow.description: Stable id. Equal to the filename without its extension — one identifier, not a mapping to keep in sync.

trigger.description: How this workflow is chosen. A classification signal picks it automatically; "explicit" means it has no signal of its own and must be named by the caller, because the difference is intent rather than anything observable in the change.

signal.description: The ClassificationInput field that selects this workflow. Required when kind is "signal".

priority.description: Order the classifier tests signals in, lowest first. Recorded so the precedence between two true signals is data rather than the order of if-statements.

level.description: The task level this workflow always produces.

requires_human_approval.description: Whether this kind of change always needs an explicit human decision, independent of the per-edge gates.

steps.description: The agents this workflow runs, in order. Order is the contract: backend-engineer precedes frontend-engineer within a phase, never the reverse.

when.description: Condition for including this step. Omitted means always. "always_sensitive" marks a workflow that forces a security pass regardless of what the caller said.
